page_title: the case for bash - Chris Dickinson

summary.title: The Case For Bash
summary.one_liner: Bash is worth learning because its core purpose is running and coordinating processes, a niche where its unusual syntax and semantics make sense.
takeaways: Bash's core data primitive is a running process, and it values running programs over variables and branching.
Bash's odd conventions, such as 0 meaning success and re-quoting variables, make sense in light of its purpose and history.
Shell pipelines like tail | awk | sort | uniq express in one line what takes much more boilerplate in Node or other languages.
Learning Bash compounds over time; the main difficulty is knowing which programs to call, not the language itself.
Other shells (Fish, Zsh, PowerShell, Nushell) share similar values, and learning Bash helps in understanding them.
summary.summary: The author argues against dismissing Bash as unmaintainable, framing it as a tool suited to a specific problem space: managing and coordinating programs. He compares a shell pipeline with an equivalent Node.js child_process example to show how much boilerplate other languages need for the same job. He explains Bash's quirks (0 as success, the [ program, re-quoting) as consequences of its values. The post closes by recommending learning Bash for daily Linux work and as a way to understand other shells, building skill gradually through one-off scripts.
